lines.text: A rock on the Riviera, held by one family for more than seven centuries, and made famous by a casino, a princess and a race. This is Monaco.
The story begins with the Grimaldis, a family of Genoa, who would one day take the rock of Monaco, legend says disguised as monks.
In 1191 Genoa began a fortress on the rock, the stones that would become the Prince's Palace.
In 1297 the Grimaldis seized it, and their family has ruled Monaco ever since.
Centuries later, in 1848, Prince Albert the First was born, an ocean scientist who would give Monaco its first constitution.
In the eighteen sixties the casino of Monte Carlo opened its doors, and gambling made the tiny state rich.
On the cliff above the sea, Albert built his Oceanographic Museum, which opened in 1910.
In 1923 Rainier the Third was born, the prince who would build Monaco into a modern state.
In 1929 cars first raced through the narrow streets and around the harbour, the Monaco Grand Prix, the most glamorous race of all.
That same year, in America, Grace Kelly was born. The Hollywood star would marry Prince Rainier in 1956.
In 1958 their son Albert was born, prince of Monaco since 2005.
And in 1997 Charles Leclerc was born, the local driver who won his home Grand Prix in 2024.
From a seized fortress to a glittering principality, Monaco still belongs to the Grimaldis.
